name: Computer Networks
description: Layers, protocols, routing algorithms, and web architecture.

articles.title: Network Architecture & Layering
articles.content:
## OSI Model (7 Layers)
1. Application (Layer 7): User interaction interface (HTTP, FTP, SMTP, DNS, SSH).
2. Presentation (Layer 6): Data representation, encryption, compression (TLS/SSL, JPEG, ASCII).
3. Session (Layer 5): Inter-host communication session establishment and teardown (NetBIOS, RPC).
4. Transport (Layer 6 -> 4): End-to-end communication, segmentation, error recovery, flow control (TCP, UDP).
5. Network (Layer 3): Packet delivery across disparate networks, logical addressing, routing (IP, ICMP, ARP).
6. Data Link (Layer 2): Node-to-node framing, physical MAC addressing, error detection via CRC (Ethernet, Wi-Fi 802.11).
7. Physical (Layer 1): Raw bit transmission over physical medium (Copper cables, Fiber optics, Hubs).

## TCP/IP Model (4 Layers)
- Application: Combines OSI layers 5, 6, and 7.
- Transport: Equivalent to OSI Layer 4.
- Internet: Equivalent to OSI Layer 3.
- Network Access: Combines OSI layers 1 and 2.

## Network Devices & PDU Mapping
| Layer | Protocol Data Unit (PDU) | Core Hardware / Addressing |
|---|---|---|
| Application | Data | Firewall (Layer 7), Gateway |
| Transport | Segment (TCP) / Datagram (UDP) | Ports ($0$ to $65535$) |
| Network | Packet | Router, Layer-3 Switch (IP Address) |
| Data Link | Frame | Layer-2 Switch, Bridge (MAC Address) |
| Physical | Bits | Hub, Repeater, Network Interface Card |

questions.q: Routing of packets between independent networks happens at which OSI layer?
questions.explanation: The Network layer uses IP addresses to determine routing paths across interconnected networks.

questions.q: What is the Protocol Data Unit (PDU) called at the Data Link layer?
questions.explanation: At Layer 2, data is encapsulated into frames containing physical MAC addresses and CRC checksums.

questions.q: A traditional Layer-2 switch forwards data frames based on which type of address?
questions.explanation: Layer-2 switches inspect destination MAC addresses within Ethernet frames to forward traffic.

questions.q: Which layer of the OSI model is directly responsible for data encryption, compression, and formatting?
questions.explanation: The Presentation layer handles formatting, syntax translation, encryption (e.g., TLS), and compression.

questions.q: At which layer of the TCP/IP model does the Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) operate?
questions.explanation: ICMP provides error reporting and diagnostics (like ping) at the Internet Layer (OSI Layer 3).

questions.q: What is the primary function of a network Hub?
options: Filter traffic based on MAC addresses
Broadcast incoming bits to all other ports
questions.explanation: A Hub operates at the Physical layer (Layer 1) and blindly floods bits received on one port to all other ports.

questions.q: Which OSI layer manages full-duplex/half-duplex session synchronization and checkpointing?
questions.explanation: The Session layer (Layer 5) manages dialogues, session checkpoints, and authorization tokens.

questions.q: How many layers are present in the standard TCP/IP original reference model?
questions.explanation: The original TCP/IP reference architecture defined 4 layers: Network Access, Internet, Transport, and Application.

questions.q: Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) translates which address type to which address type?
questions.explanation: ARP maps a known Layer-3 IP address to an unknown Layer-2 MAC address on a local segment.

questions.q: Which header field is added at the Transport layer when using TCP?
questions.explanation: The TCP header contains 16-bit source and destination port numbers for process-to-process multiplexing.

questions.q: What happens during the encapsulation process as data moves down the OSI stack?
options: Headers are removed at each layer
Headers/Trailers are added at each layer
Data is compressed into bits immediately
Encryption is applied at every single layer
questions.explanation: As data moves from Layer 7 to Layer 1, each lower layer adds its own control header (and trailer at Layer 2).

questions.q: Which protocol operates at the Data Link layer to prevent switching loops in Ethernet networks?
questions.explanation: STP operates at Layer 2 to disable redundant paths and eliminate broadcast storms/loops in switch topologies.

questions.q: What size is an IEEE 802.3 Ethernet MAC address?
questions.explanation: MAC addresses are 48-bit (6-byte) hexadecimal hardware addresses burned into NICs.

questions.q: Which of the following devices isolates broadcast domains?
questions.explanation: Routers operate at Layer 3 and do not forward Layer-2 broadcast frames by default, creating separate broadcast domains.

questions.q: What is the maximum theoretical payload size (MTU) of a standard Ethernet frame?
questions.explanation: Standard Ethernet networks have a Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) size of $1500$ bytes for the IP packet payload.

questions.q: Which layer is responsible for end-to-end error control and flow control across host endpoints?
questions.explanation: The Transport layer provides true end-to-end reliability, sliding window flow control, and segment sequencing.

questions.q: Reverse ARP (RARP) was designed to map which of the following?
questions.explanation: RARP allows diskless workstations to discover their own IP address given their MAC hardware address.

questions.q: A Layer-3 switch combines the functionality of which two network components?
questions.explanation: Layer-3 switches combine hardware-based Layer-2 switching with high-speed Layer-3 IP routing capabilities.

questions.q: Which field in an IPv4 header prevents packets from circulating indefinitely in network loops?
questions.explanation: The 8-bit TTL field is decremented by $1$ at each router hop; when TTL reaches $0$, the packet is dropped.

questions.q: PDU decapsulation occurs in which direction?
questions.explanation: Decapsulation happens on the receiving host, stripping headers layer-by-layer starting from Physical (1) up to Application (7).

articles.title: Transport Layer Protocols & Socket Mechanics
articles.content:
## TCP (Transmission Control Protocol)
- Properties: Connection-oriented, reliable, guarantees ordering, flow control, congestion control.
- Connection Management:
  - Three-Way Handshake: SYN $	o$ SYN-ACK $	o$ ACK.
  - Four-Way Termination: FIN $	o$ ACK $	o$ FIN $	o$ ACK.
- Control Mechanisms:
  - Sliding Window Protocol: Dynamic flow control preventing sender from overwhelming receiver buffer.
  - Congestion Control Algorithms: Slow Start, Congestion Avoidance, Fast Retransmit, Fast Recovery (cwnd window size).

## UDP (User Datagram Protocol)
- Properties: Connectionless, lightweight, zero connection overhead, no packet delivery or ordering guarantees.
- Use Cases: Real-time media streaming, online multi-player gaming, DNS resolution, VoIP, NTP.

## Port Allocation Ranges
- Well-Known Ports ($0 - 1023$): System services (21 FTP, 22 SSH, 25 SMTP, 53 DNS, 80 HTTP, 443 HTTPS).
- Registered Ports ($1024 - 49151$): Vendor applications (e.g., 3306 MySQL, 5432 PostgreSQL, 6379 Redis).
- Dynamic/Private Ports ($49152 - 65535$): Ephemeral client-side connection ports.

$$	ext{Socket Identifier} = 	ext{IP Address} + 	ext{Port Number}$$

questions.q: Which sequence of TCP flags correctly establishes a connection between client and server?
questions.explanation: The TCP 3-way handshake follows SYN (client), SYN-ACK (server response), and ACK (client confirmation).

questions.q: Which transport protocol is best suited for real-time multiplayer gaming where low latency is critical?
questions.explanation: UDP skips heavy handshaking and retransmissions, drastically reducing delay for time-sensitive data.

questions.q: What is the allocated numerical range for well-known server ports?
questions.explanation: Ports 0 through 1023 are reserved by IANA for standard system services.

questions.q: What standard server port does SSH (Secure Shell) listen on by default?
questions.explanation: SSH defaults to port 22. (Telnet uses 23, FTP uses 20/21).

questions.q: Which feature is natively provided by TCP but missing in UDP?
questions.explanation: TCP implements flow control using sliding windows to prevent buffer overflows at the receiver.

questions.q: What action does a host take when it receives a TCP segment targeting a closed port?
options: Sends back a TCP flag with RST
Sends back a UDP ICMP unreachable message
questions.explanation: If a port is closed, the operating system responds with a TCP packet having the RST (Reset) flag set.

questions.q: What does a socket pair consist of in a TCP connection?
questions.explanation: A full-duplex socket pair uniquely identifying a connection consists of (Source IP, Source Port, Destination IP, Destination Port).

questions.q: In TCP congestion control, what happens immediately after a packet timeout occurs?
options: Congestion window size drops to 1 MSS
questions.explanation: Upon a heavy timeout loss, TCP sets its congestion window (`cwnd`) back to $1$ Maximum Segment Size (MSS) and enters Slow Start.

questions.q: Which TCP state indicates that the local endpoint has received a FIN from the remote end and sent an ACK?
questions.explanation: In `CLOSE_WAIT`, the local host has acknowledged the remote host's `FIN` request and is waiting for the local application to close.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the TCP `TIME_WAIT` state on the active closer?
options: Allow active streams to send faster
Ensure final ACK reaches remote host and clear delayed segments
Wait for dynamic IP address renewal
questions.explanation: `TIME_WAIT` (typically 2MSL) ensures the remote side receives the final `ACK` and prevents old duplicate packets from corrupting new connections.

questions.q: What is the header overhead size of a minimum basic UDP packet?
questions.explanation: UDP headers are simple and fixed at $8$ bytes (Source Port, Destination Port, Length, Checksum). TCP headers are at least $20$ bytes.

questions.q: Which UDP port is used by DNS queries by default?
questions.explanation: Standard DNS queries and responses run over UDP port 53 (switching to TCP 53 for zone transfers or large responses).

questions.q: What is the default port for PostgreSQL database connections?
questions.explanation: PostgreSQL listens on port 5432. MySQL uses 3306, Redis uses 6379, MongoDB uses 27017.

questions.q: How does TCP handle out-of-order segments at the receiver?
options: Buffers them and uses Sequence Numbers to reconstruct order
questions.explanation: TCP tracks 32-bit Sequence Numbers, storing out-of-order segments in receiver buffers until missing segments arrive.

questions.q: What protocol is commonly used by network administrators for querying real-time system clock synchronization?
questions.explanation: NTP (Network Time Protocol) runs over UDP port 123 to synchronize clocks across nodes.

questions.q: What TCP mechanism is triggered when $3$ duplicate ACKs are received by the sender?
questions.explanation: Three duplicate ACKs signal isolated packet loss without waiting for a retransmission timer timeout, triggering Fast Retransmit.

questions.q: Which field in the TCP header is used to signal the receiver's available buffer capacity?
questions.explanation: The 16-bit Receive Window field communicates how many bytes of data the receiving node can currently buffer.

questions.q: Which port does HTTPS use for SSL/TLS encrypted traffic?
questions.explanation: HTTPS secure web communication operates on standard port 443.

questions.q: What type of attack floods target IP ports with TCP `SYN` packets without sending final `ACK`s?
questions.explanation: A SYN flood fills the server's backlog queue with half-open connections, exhausting kernel memory resources.

questions.q: Does UDP perform flow control or congestion control?
questions.explanation: UDP provides no flow control or congestion control mechanisms; applications must implement them at higher layers if needed.

articles.title: Application Layer Web Architecture & Security Protocols
articles.content:
## Web Request Lifecycle (URL Execution)
1. **DNS Lookup**: Local Cache $	o$ `/etc/hosts` $	o$ Recursive Resolver $	o$ Root Server $	o$ TLD Server $	o$ Authoritative Name Server.
2. **TCP Connection**: 3-Way Handshake on target IP (port 80/443).
3. **TLS Handshake (HTTPS)**: Cipher suite negotiation, Certificate validation, Key Exchange (ECDHE), Session Symmetric Key generation.
4. **HTTP Request & Response**: Client sends Method, Path, Headers $	o$ Server replies with Status Code, Response Headers, Body.
5. **DOM Rendering**: HTML parsing, CSSOM tree building, JS execution.

## HTTP Methods & Properties
- **Idempotency**: Repeated execution yields same server state (`GET`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, `HEAD` are idempotent; `POST` is not).
- **HTTP Status Codes**:
  - `1xx`: Informational (`101 Switching Protocols`).
  - `2xx`: Success (`200 OK`, `201 Created`, `204 No Content`).
  - `3xx`: Redirection (`301 Moved Permanently`, `302 Found`, `304 Not Modified`).
  - `4xx`: Client Error (`400 Bad Request`, `401 Unauthorized`, `403 Forbidden`, `404 Not Found`).
  - `5xx`: Server Error (`500 Internal Error`, `502 Bad Gateway`, `503 Service Unavailable`).

## Core Security Concepts
- **Symmetric Encryption**: Same key used for encryption/decryption (AES-GCM, fast).
- **Asymmetric Encryption**: Public key encrypts/verifies, Private key decrypts/signs (RSA, ECC).
- **XSS vs CSRF**:
  - **XSS (Cross-Site Scripting)**: Injected malicious scripts execute in victim browser context.
  - **CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery)**: Unauthorized commands executed on behalf of authenticated user via automated cookies.

questions.q: Which HTTP status code indicates a permanently redirected URL resource?
questions.explanation: 301 stands for Moved Permanently, directing clients and search engines to cache the new location.

questions.q: Which DNS record type maps a domain name directly to an IPv4 address?
questions.explanation: An 'A' record points a domain name to a 32-bit IPv4 address. 'AAAA' points to an IPv6 address.

questions.q: Which HTTP method is explicitly designed to be NON-idempotent?
questions.explanation: POST creates new records; executing it multiple times creates multiple distinct entity resources.

questions.q: What key component makes HTTPS secure compared to basic plain HTTP?
questions.explanation: HTTPS layers HTTP over TLS, providing encryption, data integrity, and server authentication.

questions.q: What cookie attribute prevents client-side JavaScript (e.g., `document.cookie`) from accessing sensitive session tokens?
questions.explanation: The `HttpOnly` flag hides cookies from browser scripts, protecting against XSS session hijacking.

questions.q: Which status code represents a client error when a valid user lacks permission for a resource despite being authenticated?
questions.explanation: 403 Forbidden means the server understands the caller identity but refuses authorization.

questions.q: In asymmetric cryptography used during TLS handshakes, what is the public key primarily used for?
options: Encrypting session data or verifying signatures
questions.explanation: The public key encrypts sensitive data (or validates digital signatures), which can only be decrypted by the matching private key.

questions.q: Which type of DNS server holds the official binding records for a specific domain zone?
questions.explanation: Authoritative Name Servers are the final authority holding actual DNS records (A, CNAME, MX) for domains.

questions.q: What security vulnerability occurs when an attacker tricks a user's browser into sending authenticated requests to a vulnerable web application?
questions.explanation: CSRF exploits implicit browser cookie inclusion during cross-origin state-changing requests.

questions.q: Which HTTP status code is returned when a reverse proxy server receives an invalid or timed-out response from an upstream server?
questions.explanation: 502 Bad Gateway indicates that a gateway/proxy received an invalid upstream server payload.

questions.q: What DNS record type functions as an alias pointing one domain name to another domain name?
questions.explanation: CNAME (Canonical Name) aliases a domain to another domain string instead of an explicit IP.

questions.q: Which HTTP request header informs the server about the original domain originating a Cross-Origin Request?
questions.explanation: Browsers automatically attach the `Origin` header during CORS requests to allow servers to evaluate cross-domain policies.

questions.q: Which HTTP version introduced full binary frame multiplexing over a single persistent TCP connection?
questions.explanation: HTTP/2 replaced text lines with binary frames, allowing concurrent request multiplexing over one connection.

questions.q: What HTTP status code corresponds to '304 Not Modified'?
options: Cached version is valid, no body sent
questions.explanation: 304 instructs the browser to use its cached copy, saving network bandwidth by returning an empty response body.

questions.q: What security header forces browsers to establish connection exclusively via HTTPS for a given domain?
questions.explanation: HSTS instructs browsers to automatically convert all HTTP requests to HTTPS before transmitting.

questions.q: What attack vector allows attackers to inject malicious script code into web pages viewed by other users?
questions.explanation: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) executes attacker JS scripts within the trust context of a user's browser.

questions.q: Which DNS record type specifies the mail servers responsible for accepting incoming email for a domain?
questions.explanation: MX (Mail Exchange) records specify email handling hostnames and priorities for a domain.

questions.q: HTTP/3 relies on which underlying Transport layer protocol instead of TCP?
questions.explanation: HTTP/3 uses QUIC running over UDP to eliminate TCP head-of-line blocking and speed up handshakes.

questions.q: What is the primary role of a Certificate Authority (CA) in Public Key Infrastructure (PKI)?
options: Assign IP addresses to web servers
Digitally sign and validate SSL/TLS server certificates
questions.explanation: CAs verify domain ownership and digitally sign certificates, enabling browsers to verify server identities.

questions.q: What HTTP method carries request metadata parameters inside the request body while requesting resource modification?
questions.explanation: PATCH applies partial updates to a resource, carrying modification details inside the request body.
